items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1960-01-21
items.q: The amount that I learned good when I used to play with Clarence Williams, you know.

ctx.x: Who did he play with? Just some fellas down there. I wasn't playing music then, you know. He'd play class, you know, victory balls, you know. All of them trunks, you know. I don't know. I could play manolene a little bit. The amount that I learned good when I used to play with Clarence Williams, you know. Piano, manolene, violin, and sax. That was Cindy Bessier. Yeah, he was, Cindy was a good thing. Cindy was a good thing. Cindy used to play with anybody too. You know, when he was cold out. Yeah, he didn't have…
He's trying to make the sax. He's a drummer.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-11
items.q: When I went over there with the Clarence Williams, you know, to sell that music, you know.

ctx.x: No, I said we'll ask him about that band.

No, he said I just want to ask him about that. Oh, about Charlie Love. I make Charlie Love, yeah, but my brother used to know Charlie Love. I met Charlie Love from Donisonville. And I met Charlie Love in Streetsport. When I went over there with the Clarence Williams, you know, to sell that music, you know. I met him over there, you know. Charlie Love. He's a good musician. He's from Plaquemine.
Tell him if he's from Plaquemine. He's from Plaquemine.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-11-17
items.q: I played with him after they'd get that up, him and Clarence William, you know. Clarence William had left there, you know.

ctx.x: P-Ron and Williams. Oh, you mean how long did I? Oh, I didn't play with them then. They used to go there, you know. And when we'd go off, well he'd give me a stack of music to sell, you know. He'd go to the streets, folks, and Texas, all them places, and Oklahoma, you know. And he'd give me a bunch like that to sell for, you know. But I wasn't at the place, I just used to go there sometime. I wasn't playing with him then, you know. I played with him after they'd get that up, him and Clarence William, you know.…
How did you sell that music?
